Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
307 PM EDT Fri Sep 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

Confidence has increased in a breezy and wet weekend with rain
shield reaching as far west as portions of I-81 and the Blue
Ridge Mountains. No fresh water flooding is anticipated, but 
minor coastal flooding is still expected along the lower 
Potomac River and St. Marys County. Blowout tides are expected 
elsewhere starting Saturday. Winds will strengthen tonight and 
peak Saturday afternoon. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A Nor'easter brings below normal temperatures, breezy
  conditions, and some rain at times through this weekend.

- 2) Warm and calm conditions next week before rainfall chances
  return by late next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A Nor'easter brings below normal temperatures,
breezy conditions, and some rain at times through this weekend.

Global models have come into much better agreement with respect
to the track of the Nor'easter with rain becoming increasingly
likely Saturday afternoon into Sunday. Have confidence that the
rain will reach as far west as the Blue Ridge Mountains and 
even portions of I-81 Saturday night. Quarter to half inch of 
rain expected for areas east of the Blue Ridge Mountains and an 
inch or more for areas east of I-95, particularly over northeast
Maryland. Rainfall rates will be light to moderate since 
instability will not be a concern. As for winds, wind gusts to 
around 30 mph are expected, perhaps as high as 35 mph along the 
western shore of the Chesapeake Bay. Nor'easter will begin to
exit the area Sunday night with rain chances diminishing,
although clouds will likely persist into Monday. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Warm and calm conditions next week before 
rainfall chances return by late next week.

As this weekend's Nor'easter slowly pushes offshore early next week, 
cloud cover and potential for showers diminish. High pressure builds 
in overhead briefly behind the departing Nor'easter bringing dry 
conditions to begin next week. A gradual warming trend is expected 
as highs go from low to mid 70s on Monday to around 80F Wednesday 
and Thursday. Mid-level ridging might develop across much of the 
eastern CONUS at some point during the middle to late next week. 
There's still a lot of variance in the model guidance, but if that 
were to happen we could see highs reach well into the 80s at some 
point. 

The next best chance for rain looks to be at the end of next week 
when a stronger cold front approaches from the west. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

Some LLWS is possible at western terminals as winds decouple and
winds aloft strengthen. 

Main impact will be the gusty N or NNW winds up to 25 kt
Saturday. Winds should start gradually diminishing Sat night
into Sunday, but still a little breezy. Rain is now likely at
all airports starting Sat afternoon and continuing through
Sunday. 

On Monday, VFR conditions are expected across all terminals through 
the middle of next week. Northeasterly winds persist, but reduce in 
magnitude sometime on Monday. 

&&

.MARINE...

Winds are expected to strengthen tonight through Saturday with
gale force winds likely south of Pooles Island. Gale Warnings
were expanded further north earlier today. 

Northerly winds continue to weaken below SCA criteria on Monday and 
into the middle of next week.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...

Minor coastal flooding will continue for one or two more high
tide cycles for Anne Arundel, Calvert, and Alexandria, but as
winds strengthen from the N expect blowout tides through the
weekend at those locations and locations further north on the
Chesapeake Bay. Minor coastal flooding will persist at Dahlgren
and St. Marys County for several high tide cycles. As Nor'easter
departs early next week, a snap back event may occur with 
renewd minor coastal flooding possible.
